:::{#def-lagrangian}
#### Lagrangian

For the problem of minimizing $f(\vx)$ over $\vx \in \reals^p$ subject to $\tp{\matr{A}} \vx = \vecf{b}$,
with $\matr{A}$ a $p \times m$ matrix and $\vecf{b} \in \reals^m$,
the **Lagrangian** is the function of $\vx \in \reals^p$ and $\vlagmult \in \reals^m$

$$
L(\vx, \vlagmult) \eqdef f(\vx) + \tp{\vlagmult} \paren{\tp{\matr{A}} \vx - \vecf{b}},
$$

and the entries of $\vlagmult$ are the **Lagrange multipliers**, one per constraint.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-lagrangian}
#### The gradients of the Lagrangian of a quadratic

Let $f(\vx) = \tfrac{1}{2}\,\tp{\vx} \matr{S} \vx$ with $\matr{S}$ symmetric and constant.
By the [transpose of a product](linear-algebra.qmd#thm-transpose-product),
$\tp{\vlagmult} \tp{\matr{A}} = \tp{(\matr{A} \vlagmult)}$, so

$$
\ba
L(\vx, \vlagmult)
&= \tfrac{1}{2}\,\tp{\vx} \matr{S} \vx + \tp{\vlagmult} \tp{\matr{A}} \vx - \tp{\vlagmult} \vecf{b}
&& \text{(distribute)}
\\
&= \tfrac{1}{2}\,\tp{\vx} \matr{S} \vx + \tp{(\matr{A} \vlagmult)} \vx - \tp{\vlagmult} \vecf{b},
&& \text{(transpose of a product)}
\ea
$$

and, since $\tp{\vlagmult} \paren{\tp{\matr{A}} \vx - \vecf{b}}$ is $1 \times 1$ and so equals its transpose,

$$
L(\vx, \vlagmult) = \tfrac{1}{2}\,\tp{\vx} \matr{S} \vx + \tp{\paren{\tp{\matr{A}} \vx - \vecf{b}}} \vlagmult.
$$

The partial derivatives of a sum are the sums of the partial derivatives, entry by entry.
Using the first of these forms, [derivative of a quadratic form](vector-calculus.qmd#thm-quadratic-form) for the first term,
[derivative of a linear combination](vector-calculus.qmd#cor-deriv-lincom-tp) for the second ($\matr{A} \vlagmult$ is constant in $\vx$),
and [constant with respect to a vector](vector-calculus.qmd#def-constant-wrt-vector) for the third,

$$
\ba
\deriv{\vx} L(\vx, \vlagmult)
&= \tfrac{1}{2}\,\deriv{\vx} \paren{\tp{\vx} \matr{S} \vx} + \deriv{\vx} \paren{\tp{(\matr{A} \vlagmult)} \vx} - \deriv{\vx} \paren{\tp{\vlagmult} \vecf{b}}
&& \text{(sum and constant multiple)}
\\
&= \tfrac{1}{2} \paren{2 \matr{S} \vx} + \matr{A} \vlagmult - \vzero_{p \times 1}
&& \text{(the three derivatives)}
\\
&= \matr{S} \vx + \matr{A} \vlagmult.
&& \text{(simplify)}
\ea
$$

Using the second form, in which $f(\vx)$ and $\tp{\matr{A}} \vx - \vecf{b}$ are constant in $\vlagmult$,
and [derivative of a linear combination](vector-calculus.qmd#cor-deriv-lincom-tp) again,

$$
\ba
\deriv{\vlagmult} L(\vx, \vlagmult)
&= \deriv{\vlagmult} f(\vx) + \deriv{\vlagmult} \paren{\tp{\paren{\tp{\matr{A}} \vx - \vecf{b}}} \vlagmult}
&& \text{(sum)}
\\
&= \vzero_{m \times 1} + \paren{\tp{\matr{A}} \vx - \vecf{b}}
&& \text{(the two derivatives)}
\\
&= \tp{\matr{A}} \vx - \vecf{b}.
&& \text{(simplify)}
\ea
$$

So $(\vx, \vlagmult)$ makes the gradients equal $\vzero_{p \times 1}$ and $\vzero_{m \times 1}$ exactly when

$$
\matr{S} \vx + \matr{A} \vlagmult = \vzero_{p \times 1}
\quad \text{and} \quad
\tp{\matr{A}} \vx = \vecf{b},
\qquad\text{that is,}\qquad
\underbrace{\sbmat{ \matr{S} & \matr{A} \\ \tp{\matr{A}} & \vzero_{m \times m} }}_{(p + m) \times (p + m)}
\underbrace{\sbmat{ \vx \\ \vlagmult }}_{(p + m) \times 1}
= \underbrace{\sbmat{ \vzero_{p \times 1} \\ \vecf{b} }}_{(p + m) \times 1},
$$ {#eq-kkt}

the second equation being the constraint itself.

:::
